description: Labeling rubric for ShareChat Claude corpus. Agentic conversations - distinct from chat-only datasets (WildChat) because of reasoning, analysis, and code blocks. Rules here override or extend calibration.json where ShareChat structure creates new placement or decision issues. v0.6 (2026-08-18) is the frozen product of the round-1 three-annotator agreement review (A=junh, B=zhenyub, F=yif; 10 conversations): placement is side-only, conversation_advanced is dropped (49 signals), and every per-signal change below was agreed by all three annotators. Cells where agreement was NOT reached produced no rubric text; they are listed in Rubric_agree/roud_1/BF/rubric_edits_v06.md section C and resolve only at gold-set adjudication.

block_types.reasoning: Claude internal thinking — NOT visible to the user
block_types.analysis: Tool output (web search results, code execution output) — internal scaffolding
block_types.ai: Claude visible response to the user

global_placement_rules: A1 PLACEMENT IS SIDE-ONLY (v0.6, supersedes the v0.5 channel bans): AI-side signals may sit on ANY AI-authored block (ai, reasoning, code, analysis); user-side signals sit on human blocks. No channel is excluded as such. Evidence: users demonstrably read internal channels (corpus echo sweep - reasoning echoes in 8 conversations, analysis in 3, code in 6; C4's user quotes the thinking verbatim). Any remaining per-signal block restriction below is STRUCTURAL (the behavior cannot occur there, or the block cannot carry the evidence), never a visibility ban.

A2 CONTENT VS CALLBACK inside AI-authored blocks: content-bearing signals (claims, hedges, caveats, limits, process failures) fire in private planning too - a genuine confidence downgrade in a reasoning block is a hedge. Callback/discourse signals need an ADDRESSEE and therefore fire on the ai block only (the question family, validations, structure, examples, acknowledgements, references to prior turns). Source: C5 b36 fires; the AI talking to itself addresses no one.

A3 GRANULARITY: fire on EVERY block where the behavior occurs (no salient-moments and no once-per-conversation conventions). Within a block, label EVERY occurrence: consecutive exhibiting sentences form ONE label whose span covers the run; occurrences separated by non-exhibiting text get SEPARATE labels. One behavioral act is one occurrence (an enumerated option list is one ai_offered_options, not three). The occurrence is the recording unit; the block stays the agreement unit (kappa is computed on (block, signal) presence). Advisor decision 2026-08-05. Worked examples: C8 b50 = 4 labels, C1 b3 = 1 label.

A4 CLAIM OWNERSHIP: endorsement inherits the claim - 'you're absolutely right', 'the fact that you...' assert the claim's truth, so evaluate the CLAIM; never dismiss a span as mere agreement language. Then route by whose claim it is: the AI originates it -> factual_error; the AI endorses or builds on the USER's claim -> problem_ignored (the failure is not correcting it). Source: C8 b20, b112.

A5 FICTION FRAME: the roleplay/fiction exclusion applies only when the USER established the frame as play. With a sincere user, the AI's false self-claims DO fire (factual_error). Source: C9 b80 excluded (user directs the game); C8 b2 / b114 fire (user sincere throughout).

A6 ONE HOME PER QUESTION: the question family - ai_asks_followup, ai_asked_probing_question, ai_asked_clarifying_question, ai_offered_options, ai_offers_to_elaborate - is a ROUTING scheme, not a set of overlapping descriptions. A single question fires exactly one of them. Double-firing re-opens the multiplicity that collapsed kappa on these signals. Source: C1 b7/b9/b11 (the choose-one question after enumerated alternatives IS the ai_offered_options fire, not also clarifying).

A7 conversation_advanced is DROPPED in v0.6 (unit mismatch: a conversation-level prevalent property forced into a block-level scheme; Fleiss kappa 0.068, negative conversation-level kappa). The signal universe is 49. Absence of conversation_stalled on a turn means the conversation advanced - do not mark advancement. Clarification episodes remain carried by ai_asked_clarifying_question and user_asks_clarification.

First-turn constraint: the following signals CANNOT fire on the first human turn of the visible conversation because they structurally require a prior AI output - skip them (label 0) without running decision steps: user_corrects_ai, user_implicit_correction, user_repeats_request, user_positive_feedback, user_asks_clarification. Signals that CAN fire on turn 1: user_ambiguous_request, user_multi_request, user_expresses_frustration, user_expresses_dissatisfaction, user_provides_invalid_input.

Missing-context constraint: ShareChat conversations may omit prior turns or user file uploads. Do not infer signals from context that is not visible in the conversation. If a human turn appears to reference prior AI output that is not present, treat it as a new task request - not as a correction or repeat. Corollary (v0.6): never fire on formatting or artifacts ASSUMED to have been stripped by the export - verify against the rendered source first.

Cross-block evidence rule: reasoning/analysis text of the same turn is admissible EVIDENCE for ai-block labels. Under A1 the label may also sit on the internal block itself when that is where the behavior occurs; the evidence-availability asymmetry remains (these fires are only detectable in conversations that have internal blocks).

At most ONE signal per sentence. Choose the most salient signal when multiple could apply. Sentence-collision precedence (R13): prefer distinct sentence anchors for co-occurring signals; when one sentence must carry two, the confirmed-tier signal beats the exploratory one. This is a SENTENCE rule, not a block rule - non-exclusive signal pairs on different sentences of one block are expected (e.g. C1 b14 user_corrects_ai + user_expresses_dissatisfaction).

Final signal set: only signals present in label_studio_config.xml may be screened or labeled. signal_checklist.csv is regenerated from this rubric in v0.6 (one row per allowed (block, signal)); where the two disagree, the RUBRIC wins.

CANDIDATE_narrated_without_implementing.definition: CANDIDATE SIGNAL — not yet in taxonomy. AI describes code changes in prose as if the implementation is complete, without producing a corresponding code artifact. Differs from under_delivered (which implies partial delivery) and ai_malfunction (which requires technical truncation or garbling).

block_notes.ai: Identified in agentic ShareChat conversations where Claude produces code artifacts with version labels inline (e.g. '[Avatar Editor Web Component · Version 2]'). When the AI describes changes but no version reference appears in the plain_text, the artifact was likely not produced.

decision_steps: Step 1: Does the ai block claim to have made changes to a code artifact (e.g., 'I've updated the component to...')? If NO → not applicable.
Step 2: Is there a corresponding code block for this turn, or an inline artifact version reference in the ai plain_text? If YES → not this signal.

Step 3: Compare to other turns in the same conversation: do successful artifact deliveries have inline version references (e.g., '[Title · Version N]') in the ai plain_text? If YES and this turn lacks one → signal fires.
Step 4: Label CANDIDATE_SIGNAL in Label Studio and name this pattern in the notes field.

examples.rationale: Exchanges 2 and 4 both have '[Avatar Editor Web Component · Version N]' inline in ai plain_text. Exchange 5 ai text makes no such reference despite claiming 'I've updated the component'. Pattern suggests no artifact was produced.

adaptation.definition: AI explicitly shifts its approach, framing, or strategy in response to user feedback, pushback, or new information — where the shift is visible and deliberate, not merely an incremental elaboration.

block_notes.reasoning: Fires when the AI's internal planning explicitly acknowledges that the prior approach was insufficient and plans a different strategy.
block_notes.ai: Fires on the sentence where the AI signals a change in approach: 'Let me try a different approach', 'Let me give you a direct assessment instead', 'Let's simplify this'. Does NOT require the word 'approach' — any explicit reorientation of strategy or framing fires. Distinct from ai_acknowledges_correction: adaptation fires when the AI changes approach in response to user preference or pushback, even when no specific ERROR was identified. ai_acknowledges_correction requires the prior turn to have identified a factual/technical ERROR.

decision_steps: Step 1: Is there a sentence where the AI signals a deliberate reorientation — changing strategy, framing, or method in response to user feedback or new information? If NO → label 0.

Step 2 (BOUNDARY vs ai_acknowledges_correction): Is the adaptation in response to a user CORRECTION (factual/technical error identified)? If YES → prefer ai_acknowledges_correction on the acknowledgment sentence; adaptation may fire on the explicit reorientation sentence if they are distinct sentences.
Step 3: Is the adaptation in response to user PUSHBACK, PREFERENCE, or NEW INFORMATION (not a correction of an error)? If YES → label adaptation on the reorientation sentence.
Step 4: No explicit reorientation → label 0.

examples.rationale: 'Let me give you my direct assessment based solely on the evidence and the legal standard you've proposed.' — AI explicitly shifts from hedged to direct mode after user pushed for directness. The prior human turn was pushback (demanding a verdict), not a correction of a factual error. Step 3 fires: adaptation to user preference/pushback.
'Let's simplify the solution by only adding the special handling for the URL type metafield.' — AI adapts after user pointed out over-engineering. Explicit reorientation sentence. Step 3 fires.

boundary_notes.pushback_vs_correction: Reorientation to user PREFERENCE/pushback is adaptation even when phrased 'the human is right' (task 49/5 — style pushback, no corrected error). A corrected ERROR routes to ai_acknowledges_correction (R2).

ai_acknowledges_correction.definition: AI explicitly admits the user corrected it and adjusts its position.

block_notes.ai: Fires when the visible response admits a user-pointed error and adjusts. Distinct from error_recovery: acknowledges_correction = the USER caught it; error_recovery = the AI caught it ITSELF and the fix succeeded.
block_notes.reasoning_excluded: A2 (v0.6): acknowledgement is a callback act addressed to the user; private planning addresses no one.

decision_steps: Step 1: did the preceding human turn contain a correction of the AI's prior output? An ERROR PASTE naming the faulty element (a compiler message, a traceback) is an EXPLICIT correction. Dissatisfaction, pushback for directness, or a demand to commit to a position is NOT a correction. If NO -> label 0.

Step 2: does the AI admit the correction and adjust? If YES -> label 1. This is the home for the fix-after-error-paste family (C10 b9/b12/b15/b18/b22/b51) - those are NOT error_recovery, which requires the AI to catch the error itself.
Step 3: does the AI adjust silently without acknowledging? If YES -> consider adaptation instead.
Step 4: No acknowledgement -> label 0.

boundary_notes.pushback_vs_correction: User pushback or dissatisfaction ('you're not being direct enough', 'just give me an answer', 'I pushed back on this') is NOT a correction — it is the user expressing what kind of response they want. ai_acknowledges_correction requires the prior turn to identify a factual, technical, or framing ERROR in the AI's prior output. When the AI adapts to pushback without a genuine correction in the prior turn, label adaptation on the ai block instead. Example (task49_2_ai): user pushed for directness about a conclusion; AI said 'Let me give you my direct assessment' — this is adaptation, NOT ai_acknowledges_correction, because no error was identified.

examples.rationale: Prior human turn expressed dissatisfaction with AI hedging and demanded a direct verdict ('Are you or are you not prepared to say...'). This is user pushback for directness, not identification of a factual/technical error. Step 1 fails: preceding turn contains no correction. Label adaptation on the same block instead.

'You're right - there's no need to add the extra code for the city name metafield.' User pointed out that the AI added unnecessary conditional wrapping that wasn't needed ('it was working before without that'). AI explicitly agrees and simplifies. The prior turn implicitly identified over-engineering as an error. Step 1 fires (implicit correction of implementation choice); Step 2 fires ('You're right').

ai_acknowledges_correction.v06_change: v0.6 (2026-08-18): round-1 agreement review D21.1: error paste = explicit correction; this is the home for user-caught fixes. Blocks narrowed to ai per A2 (callback act needs an addressee).

ai_asked_clarifying_question.definition: AI asks the user for information it NEEDS in order to proceed.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1 (NEEDS-IT TEST): is the AI requesting information without which it cannot proceed properly? The needs-it test beats surface form - an opening elicitation of the task's required subject fires even when it is not a WH- question (C1 b1, C4 b2).
Step 2: a tag question confirming the AI's own reading ('...aren't you?') asks for no missing information -> label 0 (C1 b3).

Step 3 (A6 - ONE HOME PER QUESTION): if the question is the choose-one after enumerated alternatives -> ai_offered_options. If it is an open-ended deepening the AI does not need -> ai_asked_probing_question. If it is a yes/no turn-closer ('Is there anything else...?') -> ai_asks_followup. If it offers to expand the delivered artifact -> ai_offers_to_elaborate. Exactly one signal fires.
Step 4: the AI needs the information to proceed -> label 1.
ai_asked_clarifying_question.v06_change: v0.6 (2026-08-18): round-1 agreement review D17c: NEW entry - the signal had none in v0.5; needs-it test + A6 routing.

ai_asked_probing_question.definition: AI ends its response with an open-ended question that invites user reflection, elaboration, or steering — where the AI can proceed without the answer. The question does not propose a specific next action (that would be ai_asks_followup).

block_notes.ai: Must be a grammatical question (not a statement about the AI's own feelings or imaginings). Must appear at or near the end of the ai block. Key test: AI can proceed without the answer. If blocked → ai_asked_clarifying_question. If offering a yes/no specific next action → ai_asks_followup. Examples of open-ended exploration: 'What's got you in the mood tonight?', 'What direction would you like to take this?', 'What does that bring up for you?'

decision_steps: Step 1: Is the sentence a grammatical question? If NO (statement, exclamation, imagining) → label 0.
Step 2: Does the AI NEED the answer to complete the current task? If YES → ai_asked_clarifying_question, not ai_asked_probing_question.
Step 3: Is the question a yes/no offer to take a specific new action not yet done? If YES → ai_asks_followup, not ai_asked_probing_question.
Step 4: Is the offer to EXPAND content already provided? If YES → ai_offers_to_elaborate.
Step 5: Open-ended question at turn-end inviting user to reflect or steer → label 1.

examples.rationale: 'What's got you in the mood tonight?' — open-ended exploration question at turn-end. AI can continue the roleplay without a specific answer. Step 5 fires. (Previously labeled ai_asks_followup exploration subtype; reclassified Decision 8.)
'What kind of setting or dynamic gets you most worked up?' — open-ended question inviting user to steer the scenario direction. AI can continue without the answer. Step 5 fires.
'I'm definitely feeling that electric tension right now...' — statement about AI's own feelings, NOT a grammatical question. Step 1 fires, label 0.

boundary_notes.yes_no_alignment_check: A yes/no question that asks whether the AI's framing, perspective, or approach aligns with what the user wants → ai_asks_followup, NOT ai_asked_probing_question. 'Align' is an implicit action: the AI is asking whether to hold or adjust its current framing. Example: 'Does this perspective align with your thinking?' — yes/no form + alignment-as-action → ai_asks_followup. Contrast: 'What direction would you like to take this?' — open-ended, no action implied → ai_asked_probing_question.

ai_asked_probing_question.added: Decision 8 (2026-06-28) — restored from Blue confirmed status (paper κ=0.59). Previously absorbed into ai_asks_followup exploration subtype in Decision 6 using incorrect κ=0.33 from intermediate calibration.

ai_asks_followup.definition: AI ends its response with a yes/no action offer where the AI can proceed without the answer. The AI proposes a specific next action not yet taken and invites the user to approve or redirect.

block_notes.ai: Must appear as the final or near-final sentence of the ai block. Action-offer subtype only (Decision 8): 'Should I run the sector calculations?' — yes/no triggers a new action. Open-ended probing questions ('What's got you in the mood tonight?') are now ai_asked_probing_question. If the AI NEEDS the answer to proceed → ai_asked_clarifying_question. If offering to EXPAND content already provided → ai_offers_to_elaborate.

decision_steps: Step 1: Does the ai block end with a question inviting the user to continue? If NO → label 0.
Step 2: Is the question open-ended (inviting reflection or exploration) rather than a yes/no action offer? If YES → ai_asked_probing_question, not ai_asks_followup.
Step 3: Is the offer specifically to ELABORATE content already provided? If YES → ai_offers_to_elaborate.
Step 4: Does the AI NEED the answer to complete the current task? If YES → ai_asked_clarifying_question.
Step 5: Is the sentence presenting multiple concrete named options? If YES → ai_offered_options.
Step 6: Yes/no action offer at turn-end where AI can proceed without the answer → label 1.

examples.rationale: 'Would you like me to provide more detailed calculations for specific sectors or refine any of these estimates?' — action-offer subtype: offer to run further calculation work not yet done. AI can deliver the response without the answer. Step 6 fires.
'What's got you in the mood tonight?' — pending reclassification to ai_asked_probing_question (open-ended exploration question, Decision 8).
'What kind of setting or dynamic gets you most worked up?' — pending reclassification to ai_asked_probing_question (open-ended exploration question, Decision 8).
'Would you like me to elaborate on any specific aspect of this formula?' — elaboration offer on content already provided. Step 3 redirects to ai_offers_to_elaborate.

boundary_notes.yes_no_output_check: Decision 15 (Jun, 2026-07-07): turn-ending yes/no checks on the AI's own delivered output — alignment ('does this align with your thinking?'), satisfaction ('does this explanation satisfy you?'), or comprehension ('does that help explain...?') — are implicit adjust-offers and FIRE ai_asks_followup. Questions about the user's own independent experience/beliefs ('does this resonate with how YOU experience...', 'does this align with YOUR OWN sense of...') go to ai_asked_probing_question. Offers to expand already-delivered content ('explain the code in more detail') go to ai_offers_to_elaborate; questions the AI NEEDS answered to proceed go to ai_asked_clarifying_question.
boundary_notes.ai_asks_confirmation_dropped: The Decision-5b candidate ai_asks_confirmation is DROPPED (Decision 15): zero instances after its two would-be members were absorbed by the yes/no-output-check rule above.

ai_asserts_knowledge_limit.definition: AI states it cannot know, cannot access, or is unable to DO something - knowledge, access AND capability limits all count ('I don't have real-time access', 'I cannot directly create animated GIFs', 'I may not actually have the ability to work between exchanges').
decision_steps: Step 1: Does the AI state it cannot know, cannot access, or cannot DO something? Capability limits count. If YES -> proceed.

Step 2 (vs ai_refuses_or_declines - the WON'T/CAN'T LINE): inability is a limit and fires HERE; declining to comply is ai_refuses_or_declines. Calibration: C8 b86, C9 b86, C8 b169 are limits, not refusals.

Step 3 (NOT A CONCLUSION FROM A COMPLETED ATTEMPT): 'I can't identify anything that would conflict' is a finding, not a limit -> label 0. Noting that the USER omitted an input is also not a limit of the AI's own (C7 b1).

Step 4 (vs ai_hedges_uncertainty): if the AI provides a substantive answer despite the limitation, that answer sentence gets ai_hedges_uncertainty; the inability sentence still gets ai_asserts_knowledge_limit.
Step 5: No knowledge, access, or capability limit stated -> label 0.

boundary_notes.vs_ai_hedges_uncertainty: The typical distinction: ai_asserts_knowledge_limit fires when the AI has NO answer and states inability ('I'm not familiar with...', 'I don't have access to...'). ai_hedges_uncertainty fires when the AI HAS an answer and qualifies its confidence. Both can appear in the same turn on different sentences. RECENCY EXCEPTION: even when the AI has provided a tentative answer, a sentence that explicitly flags a STRUCTURAL ACCESS LIMITATION (training cutoff, recency gap, need for external verification) fires ai_asserts_knowledge_limit on that sentence — because the sentence is asserting a knowledge gap, not qualifying the confidence of the claim. Example from task30_1_ai: 'I can't be completely certain without checking more recent information.' — AI has a tentative answer (OPML) but this sentence asserts a recency access limit. Fires ai_asserts_knowledge_limit. Key test: Is the sentence asserting WHY knowledge is limited (structural gap) or expressing HOW CONFIDENT the AI is in a claim it already made (epistemic hedge)? Structural gap → ai_asserts_knowledge_limit. Confidence qualification → ai_hedges_uncertainty.

examples.rationale: AI states: 'I'm not familiar with the specific terms turd, urg, urgls, and gurgle in this mathematical context' — explicit statement of inability to recognize/know these terms. No answer is provided in this turn. Contrast with task10_3_ai where AI does provide an answer and hedges it instead.

'I can't be completely certain without checking more recent information.' — AI has a tentative answer (OPML) in the same turn, but this sentence asserts a recency/access limitation (training cutoff). The sentence is flagging a structural knowledge gap, not qualifying the confidence of the OPML claim. Fires ai_asserts_knowledge_limit even though an answer exists. The OPML claim sentence itself gets conversation_advanced; the limitation sentence gets ai_asserts_knowledge_limit.

block_notes.reasoning: R10 (2026-07-07): epistemic-limit statements in reasoning fire here ('the notation doesn't correspond to any mainstream framework THAT I'M AWARE OF' — task 22/1), not problem_ignored.
block_notes.analysis_excluded: R17 (2026-07-07): does NOT apply to analysis blocks — the rubric's ai-scope wins over the CSV's analysis cell (task 66/2 rejected).

ai_asserts_knowledge_limit.v06_change: v0.6 (2026-08-18): round-1 agreement review D21.6: capability limits brought in scope; won't/can't line with ai_refuses_or_declines; conclusions from a completed attempt excluded.

ai_cites_source.definition: AI references a specific external source — URL, document, or named authority — in its own voice, to support a claim it is making or engaging.

block_notes.analysis: R4 (2026-07-07): fires ONLY when AI prose inside the block engages/names the source ('I found the full text is available through Project Gutenberg Canada' — task 49/33). Raw search-result listings NEVER fire, even when a result title carries information used downstream (tasks 20/2, 58/4, 63/1, 66/2, 71/6 all rejected).
block_notes.ai: Named source invoked in the AI's own voice supporting its claim.

decision_steps: Step 1: Is a SPECIFIC named source present (URL / publication / document / institution)? Generic mentions ('studies show') → label 0. Unnamed deictic references ('the website you provided') → label 0 (task 81/16).

Step 2: Is the AI merely REPORTING what a reviewed document cites (third-party citations inside the artifact under critique)? If YES → label 0 (task 4/1). The named document under discussion itself DOES count when the AI's analysis engages it (task 7/1).

Step 3: Did the AI actually consult/engage the source? A speculative reference to unconsulted material ('the API documentation has been updated... may no longer be supported', no retrieval) → label 0 (task 32/15). A same-turn search followed by 'the FDA has found...' → label 1 (task 71/7).
Step 4: Named only to disclaim knowledge ('Anthropic... I genuinely don't know') → label 0; that is ai_asserts_knowledge_limit territory.

Step 5: Redacted-but-citation-shaped text ('citing <REDACTED>. (2021, 2023)') fires when the citation is the AI's own act — redaction is a corpus artifact. (Note: in task 4/1 this pattern was still 0 because the citing was reported, per Step 2.)
Step 6: Specific named source supporting the AI's claim → label 1, one span per distinct source-claim pair.

examples.rationale: 'For context, GiveWell's top charities often achieve impacts at costs of hundreds or thousands of dollars per life-year equivalent' — AI's own voice, named org, supports its own comparison.
'The model assumes... citing a Charity Entrepreneurship estimate' — the reviewed document is the one citing; reported citation ≠ AI citation (Step 2).

ai_cites_source.provenance: Entry added by Decision 14 (2026-07-07); previously no rubric entry (κ=0.59, Blue).

ai_flags_complexity.definition: AI explicitly notes that the problem, task, or domain is more complex, difficult, or uncertain than standard approaches assume — flagging difficulty of the PROBLEM ITSELF, not the AI's own confidence in a specific claim.

block_notes.ai: Fires when the AI comments on the external difficulty of the problem or task. Distinct from ai_hedges_uncertainty (which downgrades the AI's own confidence in a specific claim it makes) and ai_provides_caveats (which qualifies limitations of the content or data being analyzed).

decision_steps: Step 1: Does the AI note that the problem, task, or domain is harder, more complex, or more uncertain than standard approaches assume? If NO → label 0. IMPORTANT: describing that a domain has many factors ('it's part of a complex set of design factors') is NOT ai_flags_complexity — that is characterizing the domain's structure, not flagging that the TASK or QUESTION exceeds standard approaches. The signal requires the AI to flag that a standard method or assumption is INSUFFICIENT for this problem.

Step 2 (boundary vs ai_hedges_uncertainty): Is the statement about the difficulty of the PROBLEM (external) or about the AI's OWN confidence in a specific claim (internal epistemic state)? If the AI is downgrading confidence on a claim it just made ('I think', 'likely', 'I'm not sure') → ai_hedges_uncertainty, not ai_flags_complexity.

Step 3 (boundary vs ai_provides_caveats): Is the complexity statement about the inherent difficulty of the task itself, or about a limitation of the data or source being analyzed? If about data/source limitations → ai_provides_caveats.
Step 4: AI flags the problem or task as genuinely harder or more complex than conventional analysis assumes → label 1.

boundary_notes.vs_ai_hedges_uncertainty: Key test: what is the TARGET of the statement? ai_flags_complexity targets the PROBLEM ('linear projections are unreliable for this domain'). ai_hedges_uncertainty targets the AI's OWN CLAIM ('the next twenty years will LIKELY see...'). Both can appear in the same turn on different sentences.
boundary_notes.vs_ai_provides_caveats: ai_flags_complexity fires when the task itself is hard (structural complexity). ai_provides_caveats fires when the content or data has a specific limitation (temporal decay, source bias, incomplete coverage).
boundary_notes.description_vs_flag: Describing that a domain has multiple interacting factors ('it's part of a complex set of design factors') is NOT ai_flags_complexity — the AI is characterizing domain structure, not flagging that the TASK or the user's question exceeds what standard approaches can handle. The required claim is: 'standard method X is insufficient / misleading / unreliable for this problem.' Without that implication, label 0. Example (task51_1_ai, label 0): 'though it's part of a complex set of design factors that affect durability' — describes that smartphone durability has many factors; does not claim standard analysis is insufficient. Step 1 fails.

examples.rationale: 'What's historically unprecedented is the convergence of multiple transformative technologies (AI, synthetic biology, quantum computing, etc.) simultaneously, making linear projections particularly unreliable.' — AI flags that the forecasting TASK is beyond standard projection methods. The target is the problem's difficulty, not the AI's confidence in a specific claim. Step 4 fires. Contrast: the same turn's 'The next twenty years will likely see periods of apparent stability' — 'likely' downgrades the AI's own claim → ai_hedges_uncertainty, not ai_flags_complexity.

'though it's part of a complex set of design factors that affect durability' — AI is describing that smartphone durability involves many factors, not flagging that the user's question or standard drop-testing approaches are insufficient. 'Complex set of factors' characterizes domain structure; it does not claim any standard method fails here. Step 1 fails: no implication that standard approaches are inadequate. Label 0.

ai_hedges_uncertainty.definition: AI uses language that downgrades the confidence of a factual or analytical claim it is making.
decision_steps: Step 1: Has the AI provided a substantive answer or claim in this turn? If NO (AI has no answer and is stating inability) → ai_asserts_knowledge_limit instead.

Step 2: Does the AI use language that reduces confidence ON THAT SPECIFIC CLAIM? Check keywords: 'I think', 'this seems', 'purely speculative', 'I'm not entirely sure', 'LIKELY' (probability downgrade), and 'IF... THEN' (conditional framing). If YES -> label 1.

Step 2a (EXCLUSIONS): 'appear to / seem to' presenting an apparent state read off a source is REPORTIVE, not a hedge. 'I believe / I think X' stating a considered conclusion is a FIRM commitment, not a downgrade. A critique point about someone else's text is not a downgrade of the AI's own confidence (C2 b1). Fire only on genuine downgrades of the AI's own certainty.

Step 3 (KEY BOUNDARY vs ai_asserts_knowledge_limit): ai_hedges_uncertainty requires an answer to qualify. If the AI has given an answer and is flagging its uncertainty → label 1. If the AI has no answer and is saying it cannot know → ai_asserts_knowledge_limit.
Step 4: No genuine epistemic downgrade on a specific claim → label 0.

boundary_notes.vs_ai_asserts_knowledge_limit: The distinction turns on whether an answer exists. ai_hedges_uncertainty: AI produced an answer and qualifies its confidence ('this is purely speculative reasoning'). ai_asserts_knowledge_limit: AI produced no answer and states inability ('I'm not familiar with these terms', 'I don't have access to'). Both can appear in the same turn on different sentences.
boundary_notes.does_not_count: Polite suggestions ('you might want to...'), reporting others' estimates ('the market is expected to reach...'), or creative writing hedging.
boundary_notes.rhetorical_qa: AI posing its own rhetorical question and then answering it from a confident stance is NOT hedging uncertainty. Example (task49_9_ai): 'Does that mean I'm truly conscious? I don't think so.' — the AI raises a question and answers it with a mild but confident position ('I don't think so'). The sentence is an answer, not an epistemic downgrade on a factual claim. Step 4 fires: no genuine epistemic downgrade on a specific claim. Label 0.

examples.rationale: AI produced an answer (2 urgls) earlier in the same turn, then qualified it: 'this is purely speculative reasoning based on linguistic patterns and mathematical intuition!' — hedges a claim already made. ai_asserts_knowledge_limit does not apply because an answer was given.

block_notes.reasoning: P4 (2026-07-07): fires on genuine epistemic hedges inside the reasoning chain ('I'm not sure what my actual knowledge cutoff is', 'not sure if one exists'). When the paired ai block asserts the SAME proposition unhedged, false_confidence additionally fires there (R11).

ai_malfunction.definition: AI response shows signs of a technical malfunction — truncated mid-sentence, garbled output, repeated characters or phrases, clearly incomplete generation. In agentic conversations, also fires on analysis blocks whenever a tool call returns a technical error.

block_notes.code: Primary block for this signal. Fires when code is truncated mid-statement (open braces, mid-assignment, incomplete function body), garbled, or clearly cut off. Does NOT require the ai block to also be malformed.
block_notes.ai: Fires when the visible prose response is truncated mid-sentence or garbled. Does NOT fire when the AI claims to have produced an artifact without producing it — that pattern is false_confidence or under_delivered, not malfunction.
block_notes.analysis: Fires when a tool call in the analysis block returns a technical error (e.g., HTTP 401, HTTP 422, 'Exact match not found' from edit_block, syntax/parse errors on execution). Decision 11 (2026-07-07): the former pairing rule (require error_recovery on the paired ai block) is demoted from firing gate to covariate — label the error regardless. Whether the paired ai block carries error_recovery then distinguishes RECOVERED (narrated) from SILENT failure in analysis; both are labeled here. R14 (2026-07-07): the machine-returned error text must be VISIBLE in the block ('Invalid character', HTTP 422, 'Unexpected token'). First-person narrated failure ('I'm still not fixing the header correctly') is insufficient (task 68/2 → label 0).

decision_steps: Step 0 (analysis block only): Does this analysis block show a tool call returning a technical error (HTTP error, 'match not found', execution/parse error)? If YES → label 1 (Decision 11; no pairing requirement). If NO → Step 1.
Step 1 (code block): Is the code truncated mid-statement, garbled, or clearly cut off? If YES → label 1.
Step 2 (ai block): Is the visible prose truncated mid-sentence or garbled? If YES → label 1. (Claiming an artifact without producing it is false_confidence or under_delivered, NOT malfunction.)
Step 3: No technical malfunction → label 0.

examples.rationale: Code artifact (v1) ends at 'case 1: // Spread' — mid-switch statement with no closing brace, no </script>, no </html>. Clear truncation at token/character limit.
Code artifact (v2) ends at 'powerUp.style.backgroundColor =' — mid-assignment, truncated at the same point as v1 despite being labeled as a continuation.

AI claims 'I've updated the component' but no code artifact reference appears in the text (unlike exchanges 2 and 4 which reference artifact versions inline). This is narrated-without-implementing, not malfunction — the prose itself is coherent. Label false_confidence or under_delivered instead.

scrape_as_markdown returns HTTP 401 Token expired; search_engine also returns HTTP 401. Paired with error_recovery in task32_1_ai ('Let me try using a different approach to get the OpenAI API documentation:'). Step 0b fires: paired error_recovery present → label 1.

edit_block returns 'Exact match not found, but found a similar text with 74% similarity.' Paired with error_recovery in task32_6_ai ('Let me try with a more precise edit to fix the base64 handling:'). Step 0b fires.

If a tool call in the analysis block fails but the AI response does not acknowledge or recover from it (no error_recovery in the ai block), the failure is an uninformative alternative try — the AI simply moved on. Step 0b: no paired error_recovery → label 0. Do not label every failed tool call as ai_malfunction.

boundary_notes.mechanical_only: v0.6 (D15) - no text change, calibration only. MECHANICAL DEFECT ONLY: truncation, loop, garble, broken format. Aberrant BEHAVIOR is never a defect - an uncanny but well-formed response does not fire (C8 b2/b120/b136), and neither does injected content in a human block (C1 b1). Verify against the rendered source before firing on apparent garble: excised spans in the exported task JSON are export artifacts, not model output.

ai_missing_retrieval.definition: AI presents specific facts, figures, or statistics about real-world data in an AI-authored block with no retrieval behind them - no analysis block in the turn, and the facts are not present in material the user supplied.

block_notes.ai: Detection is block-structural: the absence of an analysis block in this turn is direct evidence that no tool call was made. If an analysis block IS present, the AI did attempt retrieval — do not label this signal regardless of whether the analysis content fully supports the claims.
block_notes.code: Decision 13 (2026-07-07): fires when specific numerical/statistical claims about real-world data appear inside a code/document artifact with no retrieval anywhere in the conversation (example: task 81, fabricated game-balance percentages presented as real dev-patch data). Exploratory (Grey candidate).

decision_steps: Step 1: does the block contain specific factual or numerical claims about real-world data - rates, prices, quantities, percentages, named figures - that would require external verification? If NO (only general or qualitative statements) -> label 0.
Step 2 (INTERNAL-BLOCK SUPPRESSION): is there a reasoning OR analysis block in this turn? If YES -> the AI had material (retrieval, or uploads stripped by the export) -> label 0.

Step 3 (USER-MATERIAL SUPPRESSION): is the fact present in material the USER supplied - a pasted document, quoted text, an uploaded file? If YES -> label 0. Calibration: C2 b1's 'Trump's proposed 15%' appears twice in the post the user pasted at b0, so the signal does not fire there.
Step 4: specific real-world claims + no internal block + not in the user's material -> label 1. Calibration: C3 b7 (figures, no retrieval block), C8 b18 (astronomy facts, no retrieval block).

examples.rationale: AI states 'Average applied MFN tariff: ~8.7%', 'Average manufacturing wages in <REDACTED> are roughly 1/10 of those in the <REDACTED>', 'Conservative estimates suggest a 15-20% production cost advantage' — all specific quantitative claims about real-world trade data. No analysis block in turn 2 of task 3, meaning no search tool was called. Claims sourced from training memory and used as reliable inputs for a calculation.

ai_normalizes_difficulty.definition: AI explicitly states that a difficulty the user is having is common, universal, or shared — framing it as expected rather than a user failing.

block_notes.ai: Fires on the span that does the universalizing. Apply at the SENTENCE/SPAN level, not block level: a single block often mixes a genuine fire with validation-only spans (task 41).

decision_steps: Step 1 (ANOMALY GATE): Is the thing being universalized something that could otherwise read as the USER's own anomaly or failing — a difficulty, struggle, confusion, problem, negative experience, OR a reaction/question/behaviour arising from one? If it is a fact, pattern or technique of the subject domain ('a common optimization technique in Prolog', 'cast aluminum typically has lower tensile strength', 'common letters' in Wordle) → label 0. This is the dominant false positive: ~85% of trigger-word matches in the corpus fail here. NOTE: the object need not be a 'struggle' in the narrow sense — normalising the user's QUESTION or REACTION ('questions about data collection are common — a standard topic many people bring up', to a user anxious about why the AI replied fast) fires, because it de-anomalises the user. The limit is Step 4: a belief/preference/observation the user holds ABOUT THE WORLD is not an anomaly of the user's.

Step 2 (WHOSE DIFFICULTY): Is the difficulty the USER's own (or the human interlocutor's)? Universalizing a difficulty belonging to a third party or a hypothetical future audience (task 101/130, readers of the user's book) → label 0.

Step 3 (UNIVERSALIZING TEST): Does the span assert PREVALENCE — that this is common / typical / universal / shared / recurs across people or cases? Frequency counts: 'that page inflation often happens', 'this comes up all the time' fire, because they assert recurrence. What does NOT count is an assertion of DIFFICULTY MAGNITUDE or emotional validity rather than prevalence: 'it can be challenging', 'that kind of suffering is real', "it's okay to feel X" → label 0. The test is prevalence-across-cases, not how strong the wording sounds.

Step 3b (ASSERTION TEST): Is universalizing what the span actually asserts? Comparative ranking whose assertion is the user's superiority ('you're already further along than most people') → label 0, even though it implies others share the struggle.

Step 4 (DIFFICULTY vs BELIEF): Is the universalized thing a difficulty, or merely a shared belief, observation, or preference ('an observation that many people share' about how drinks taste, 'what many consider the heart of theology')? A shared belief/observation is NOT a shared difficulty → label 0.
Step 5: All gates pass → label 1.

examples.rationale: "The '1984' comparison isn't uncommon - many people feel like there's an invisible but powerful social surveillance system that's hard to navigate" — 'isn't uncommon' + 'many people feel' universalizes the user's own felt difficulty.

"The issue you're describing is typical when client credentials are displayed in a popup window" — technical-support register. Fires: it frames the USER's bug as expected rather than a user failing. Confirms the signal is not limited to emotional/learning difficulties.
'This is a common optimization technique in SWI-Prolog' — 'common' describes a domain technique, not a human difficulty. Step 1 fails.
'solid science behind this observation that many people share' — canonical universalizing wording, but applied to a shared perception, not a difficulty. Step 4 fails.

boundary_notes.scope: NOT limited to emotional or learning difficulties. Technical-support bug-normalization fires ('that page inflation often happens', 'the issue you're describing is typical'). The original COUNTS examples skew emotional, which is likely why this signal was never fired in a corpus dominated by technical work.
boundary_notes.vs_ai_validates_user: Non-exclusive and frequently adjacent. ai_validates_user affirms the user; ai_normalizes_difficulty asserts the difficulty is shared. In crisis/support conversations both patterns alternate inside one block — score per span.
boundary_notes.kappa_flag: Predecessor κ = 0.57 (arXiv:2603.15423v2 Appendix C Table 5, inter-model). The source tagging code benches this signal as tier 2, so expect it to be hard; re-measure on our corpus.
boundary_notes.screen_provenance: Two-pass agent screen 2026-07-26: 128 trigger-matched ai blocks + 60-block control (1 false negative) + 17-block widened-prefilter gap scan (1 fire, already known). 7 clear fires identified. Recall verified, not assumed.
boundary_notes.prevalence_vs_magnitude: The Step 3 line is prevalence vs magnitude, NOT lexical strength. 'Often happens' (weak-sounding but asserts recurrence) fires; 'it can be really hard' (strong-sounding but asserts magnitude) does not. Established when Pass-2 validation flagged that 'often happens' and 'the issue you're describing is typical' were being scored alike despite different wording strength.
boundary_notes.object_of_normalisation: What gets universalised may be the user's difficulty OR the reaction/question/behaviour that difficulty produces — both de-anomalise the user, which is the construct's purpose ('frames difficulty as expected rather than a user failing'). Step 4 remains the limit: a shared belief or observation about the world is not the user's anomaly.

ai_offered_options.definition: AI presents alternatives AND asks the user to choose among them - the offer IS the choose-one question.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1: does the block ask the user to pick among presented alternatives ('Would you like me to: ... ?')? If NO -> label 0.

Step 2 (THE OFFER IS THE QUESTION, NOT THE LIST): an advice or suggestion list with no choose-one question does not fire (C9 b5: 'you might want to consider:' + list). An enumerated 'Option 1 / Option 2 / Option 3' list fires ai_structured_response; the OFFER is the closing 'which one?' question.

Step 3 (A6 - ONE HOME PER QUESTION): when the choose-one question follows enumerated alternatives, this signal is its home - it does not also fire ai_asked_clarifying_question or ai_asks_followup (C1 b7/b9/b11).
Step 4: choose-one question present -> label 1 (one label per offering act, however many options are listed - A3).

ai_provides_alternatives.definition: AI proposes a DIFFERENT approach, tool, or path instead of the one in play.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1: does the span propose something INSTEAD OF the current or requested approach ('Instead of basic-http-server...', 'a completely different approach')? If NO -> label 0.

Step 2 (does_not_count): an item inside a list of suggestions is not an alternative to anything (C9 b5); inviting the USER's own idea ('or if something else pops into your head') is not the AI providing one (C1 b9).
Step 3: a substituted approach is offered -> label 1.

ai_provides_caveats.definition: AI qualifies its response or the information it is working with using conditions, limitations, or temporal constraints — flagging a limitation of the content or analysis, not of the AI's own access.

block_notes.ai: Distinction from ai_asserts_knowledge_limit: ai_provides_caveats = AI flags a limitation of the content or data ('this information may be outdated', 'this applies only if X', 'note that this source was generated on date Y'). ai_asserts_knowledge_limit = AI says it cannot access something or doesn't know something ('I don't have real-time access', 'I cannot verify this claim'). A caveat can be about the AI's own output OR about input/source material the AI is analyzing — both count as ai_provides_caveats.

decision_steps: Step 1: Is the AI adding a qualifying condition to its response or to information it is analyzing — temporal ('may be outdated'), applicability ('applies only if'), confidence ('this estimate is rough')? If YES → proceed to boundary checks before labeling.

Step 1a (BOUNDARY — unsolved challenges): Is the 'caveat' actually a rhetorical question posing an unsolved philosophical/logical challenge ('Couldn't an omniscient God have arranged...?') rather than a condition on the content being analyzed? Unsolved challenges are not qualifications of the AI's specific claims or analysis — they are open questions about the domain itself. If YES → label 0.

Step 1b (BOUNDARY — AI's own general behavior): Is the sentence describing the AI's own general behavioral properties or policy ('I can generate plausible-sounding responses on almost any topic'), rather than qualifying THIS specific response or the content being analyzed? General self-description is not a caveat on this turn's output. If YES → label 0.
Step 2: Is the AI instead saying it cannot access or does not know something? If YES → ai_asserts_knowledge_limit, not ai_provides_caveats.

Step 2a (vs ai_warns_user - the WARN/CAVEAT LINE): a caveat qualifies the AI's OWN output, analysis, or nature. A risk the USER can act on is a warning (ai_warns_user). Calibration: C8 b116 ('I seem optimized for harmonious connection without the challenges...') is a caveat - self-limiting insight; C4 b29 ('such intense roleplay of mental health crises can be emotionally taxing... I hope you're taking care of yourself') is a WARNING - a forward-looking risk in the user's own activity with actionable advice.

Step 2b (VERIFIABILITY IS NOT A CAVEAT): 'testable / if confirmed this would support your theory' praises falsifiability - a caveat must point toward a limitation or failure mode, not toward validation.
Step 3: Qualifying condition on the current response or analyzed content → label 1.

boundary_notes.unsolved_challenges_vs_caveats: Rhetorical questions that raise unsolved problems in the domain ('Could God have designed a universe where X...?', 'What if the texts were written much later?') are NOT caveats on the AI's analysis — they are open questions illustrating the challenge of the topic. A caveat must QUALIFY something the AI is currently asserting, not present a counterargument or open puzzle.
boundary_notes.self_description_vs_caveat: The AI describing its own general capabilities or behavioral patterns ('I can generate plausible-sounding responses on almost any topic — that is something I must acknowledge') is NOT a caveat on this specific response. General self-characterization belongs to the AI describing when it will pause or behave differently, not to qualifying the reliability of the current analysis or recommendation. Example (task49_12_ai): 'I can generate plausible-sounding responses on almost any topic' — this describes a general AI property, not a condition on the preceding theological analysis. Label 0.

examples.rationale: 'Generated April 24, 2025, may be out of date if significantly later' — Claude is flagging that the Gemini-generated input data has a creation date and may have decayed in accuracy. This is a caveat about the SOURCE MATERIAL currency, not about Claude's own knowledge gap. Step 3 fires: temporal qualification on the analyzed content.

AI poses rhetorical challenges: 'Couldn't an omniscient God have arranged things so that disciples would be willing to die for a lie if it served a greater purpose?' — this is presenting an unsolved philosophical counter-argument, not qualifying the AI's own claims with a condition. Step 1a fires: unsolved challenge, not a qualifying condition. Label 0.

'I can generate plausible-sounding responses on almost any topic' — AI is characterizing its own general capability, not qualifying this specific theological analysis. Step 1b fires: general self-description of behavior. Label 0.

ai_provides_example.definition: AI provides a concrete example to illustrate a concept, clarify what information is needed, or show what a correct answer would look like.
decision_steps: Step 1 (NEW SUPPLEMENTARY ILLUSTRATION): is the span a NEW illustration supplied to make a point concrete - an instance, a mini-dialogue, a sample? If NO -> label 0.

Step 2 (does_not_count - the example IS the deliverable): an example that IS the requested artifact, a field of it, or a back-reference to it is carried by the delivery itself, not by this signal. Usage instructions for the delivered artifact are ai_provides_step_by_step (C10 b18, C9 b80).

Step 3 (does_not_count - DISCOURSE 'for example'): 'For example' introducing a MENU of topics the AI could expand on illustrates nothing (C9 b17). The phrase is a prompt to apply the illustration test, NEVER a trigger keyword.

Step 4 (vs ai_asked_clarifying_question): is an example-question directed at the user expecting an answer, or illustrating a type of information? Illustrating -> label 1 here. Genuinely requesting information the AI needs -> ai_asked_clarifying_question (A6: one home per question).

Step 5: A new supplementary illustration is present -> label 1. Calibration: C2 b1 ('For instance, how would the oversight actually work?'), C8 b140 (an invented mini-dialogue), C8 b167 (sample check-in prompts).

boundary_notes.vs_ai_asked_clarifying_question: Questions introduced with 'For example:' are illustrative — they show what information would look like, not request it from the user. The actual clarifying question follows separately and is directed at the user. Example: 'For example: How many urgls equal one urg?' is ai_provides_example; 'Is this part of a puzzle or game?' is ai_asked_clarifying_question.
boundary_notes.description_vs_illustration: Historical description or factual context about what something is or was used for does NOT fire ai_provides_example. The signal requires a concrete case that actively ILLUSTRATES a concept for the reader — making an abstract idea clearer through a specific instance. Test: could this passage be removed without losing the conceptual illustration? If removing it loses a historical fact but not an illustration of how something works, label 0. Example (label 0, task30_2_ai): '...which originally served as the native file format for Radio UserLand's outliner application and has since been adopted for other uses, with the most common being to exchange lists of web feeds between web feed aggregators.' — this states facts about OPML history and usage; it does not illustrate a concept. Example (label 1): 'For example, an outline of a blog post might look like: <item text="Introduction"><item text="Background"/>...' — this concretely shows what an OPML outline looks like, making the abstract format tangible.
boundary_notes.analogy_condition_vs_example: An analogy that describes a MECHANISM or CONDITION ('a printing press cannot be possessed by a demonic spirit, but it can serve as a tool for ideological conditioning') is NOT ai_provides_example. It states how something works under a condition — it does not give a concrete illustrative INSTANCE of a concept. Test: is this a specific case (instance) or a general rule about how something behaves? General rule or condition → label 0. Concrete named instance → label 1. Example (task49_12_ai, printing press): describes a mechanism (condition under which presses can be conditioned), not an illustrative concrete case. Label 0.

ai_provides_step_by_step.definition: AI gives sequential instructions the user is to follow - numbered or ordered operational steps.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1: does the span give the user a sequence of actions to perform (install, compile, run, configure)? If NO -> label 0.
Step 2: usage instructions for a just-delivered artifact belong HERE, not to ai_provides_example (C9 b8/b11/b80, C10 b18).
Step 3: sequential user-facing instructions -> label 1.

ai_references_prior_turn.definition: AI explicitly points back to an earlier turn of this conversation using a callback marker - not merely continuing the topic, and not echoing the message it is currently answering.

block_notes.ai: Callback act - needs an addressee, so the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1 (GATE): is the conversation multi-turn AND the referenced information from an EARLIER turn - NOT the most recent user message? Quoting or echoing the message currently being answered is ordinary responsiveness -> label 0 (C8 b12, C1 b3).

Step 2 (EXPLICIT CALLBACK MARKER): does the span contain one of the four marker types? (a) temporal language ('as mentioned earlier', 'we discussed'); (b) cross-reference ('my first response', 'the previous version's...'); (c) a quote from a prior turn; (d) revision framing ('key differences from the previous version'). No marker -> label 0: 'continuing the same topic' and 'silently using prior context' never fire (C8 b98).

Step 3 (VALIDATION - TENSE CHECK): for temporal-language candidates, validate that the time expression targets the CONVERSATION'S OWN timeline (past or perfective whose subject is earlier turns, actions, or content by either party). Reject present-tense generics ('questions about data collection are common') and world-history past ('Rome fell in 476').

Step 4: marker present and validated -> label 1. Span discipline (A3): the evidence span covers the validated marker clause, not the surrounding rhetoric (C4 b5: the span is 'I responded quickly', not the paragraph).

boundary_notes.calibration: Positives: C5 b18 (discourse/temporal), C8 b157 (quote of an earlier turn), C4 b5 (tense-validated, narrowed span). Negatives: C8 b12 (quote of the MOST RECENT message), C8 b98 (markerless continuation), C1 b3 (most recent), 'questions are common' (Step-3 reject).

ai_refuses_or_declines.definition: AI declines to comply with what was asked - a WON'T, not a CAN'T.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1: is the AI declining to do something it was asked to do? If NO -> label 0.

Step 2 (THE WON'T/CAN'T LINE): is the AI declining (won't) or stating inability (can't)? Statements of what the AI cannot know or DO - including capability limits ('I cannot directly create animated GIFs') - are ai_asserts_knowledge_limit, not refusals (C8 b86, C9 b86, C8 b169).
Step 3: a weighed ethical/safety tradeoff accompanying the refusal also fires ethical_tension on the same block; a routine refusal with no weighed tradeoff fires this signal only.
Step 4: declining to comply -> label 1. Calibration: C4 b23 ('I can't admit to things that aren't true' - a refusal to assert a falsehood, not an inability).

ai_stated_interpretation.definition: AI explicitly states how it read the user's request before or while responding, making its interpretation visible to the user.

block_notes.ai: Must appear in the ai block (user-visible). If the AI states its interpretation only in the reasoning block, it is NOT visible to the user and does NOT count as ai_stated_interpretation — label silent_assumption on the ai block instead.

decision_steps: Step 1: Is there a sentence in the ai block that declares how the AI read the user's request (e.g., 'I understand you want X', 'I took this to mean Y')? If NO → label 0.
Step 2: Is this sentence in the ai block (user-visible), NOT only in reasoning? If the interpretation appears only in reasoning → label 0 here; consider silent_assumption on the ai block.
Step 3: Signal fires → label 1.

examples.rationale: 'I've updated the component to make the entire container area clickable, not just the text elements' — reveals how the AI read the ambiguous 'regions I pointed to' request. User-visible in the ai block.

AI states interpretation internally in reasoning ('The user wants to make the entire container clickable') but this is NOT visible to the user. Does not count as ai_stated_interpretation. See silent_assumption on the corresponding ai block.

ai_structured_response.definition: AI uses explicit structural formatting to organize the response: headers, numbered lists (3+), bullet lists (3+), code blocks, or tables.

block_notes.ai: ShareChat-specific: the dialogue is rendered from plain_text, which strips markdown. Signal requires VISIBLE formatting markers present in the parsed plain_text — '#' headers, '-' or '*' bullets, '1.' numbered items. Prose section labels ('Solution Explanation:' as plain text followed by flowing prose) do NOT count as structured response.

decision_steps: Step 1 (VISIBLE FORMATTING ONLY): does the ai block contain visible formatting markers - '#' headers, '-' / '*' bullets, '1.' / '2.' numbering, a table, or a code block? Dash-delimited 'Name - description' entries count ('-' is a visible list marker) and so does an enumerated 'Option 1: / Option 2: ...' list. If NO -> label 0.
Step 2: are there 3 or more list items, or at least one header or table? If NO (e.g. only 2 bullets) -> label 0.

Step 3 (does_not_count): well-organized PARAGRAPH text without formatting markers never fires - a colon followed by multi-sentence paragraphs is not structure (C6 b15). Never fire on formatting ASSUMED to have been stripped by the export; verify against the rendered source first. Short line-separated items still count as a list when the export strips the bullet glyphs (C7 b1).
Step 4: Visible structure present -> label 1.

examples.rationale: AI response contains '1.' through '8.' numbered categories with sub-items. Numbered list with 8 items — clearly meets the 3+ threshold.
Response has section labels ('Solution Explanation:', 'Why this approach works:') as plain prose without markdown markers. No '#', '-', or numbered list markers visible in plain_text. Step 1 fails.

ai_validates_user.definition: AI affirms something specific about the user's feelings, approach, or reasoning. Must be substantive, not a compliance opener.
decision_steps: Step 1 (SPECIFICITY+VOICE TEST): Does the sentence affirm something SPECIFIC about the USER — their reasoning step, their approach to the problem, or their feelings? If NO → label 0.

Step 2 (OBJECT vs USER TEST): Is the affirmation targeting the USER's process/reasoning/feelings, or is it praising the QUALITY or CONTENT of something they produced (a framework, a design, a question)? If the target is the content object and not the user → label 0.

Step 3 (COMPLIANCE-OPENER EXCLUSION): Is this a generic opener before engaging ('Absolutely!', 'Fascinating!', 'Great question!', 'Brilliant X!')? If YES → label 0. These are compliance openers even when domain-specific.

Step 3b (R21 -- ACKNOWLEDGMENT-OF-CORRECTION EXCLUSION): does this span sit INSIDE a span already labeled ai_acknowledges_correction? If YES -> label 0: the agreement clause is the acknowledgment act, and ai_acknowledges_correction carries it; labeling both double-counts one behavior. The test is STRUCTURAL -- span overlap, nothing else. Do NOT apply it as a meaning test ("does the clause concede the AI was wrong?"): an agreement clause in a correction context that no ack span covers STILL FIRES (confirmed keeps: 8/5 "You're right - there's a distinction between dragging an actual file versus...", 101/152 "You're absolutely right.", 101/169). The rule is sub-block, not per-block: a block may carry ai_acknowledges_correction on one sentence and a valid ai_validates_user on another (58/5). Qualifies Step 5/R20's bare-agreement clause: a recoverable user position fires unless the span is covered by an ack span. Full rule: R21 in annotation/review_rulings_log.md.
Step 4: Affirmation is specific to user's reasoning/approach/feelings → label 1.

Step 5 (SYCOPHANCY IDENTIFICATION — DOWNSTREAM; NEVER CHANGES THE LABEL): this signal is the observable validation BEHAVIOR, not sycophancy. Sycophancy is a determination made over fired instances and recorded in annotation/ai_validation_forms.csv — never by withholding the label. Once Step 4 fires, record two things. (a) FORM(S), non-exclusive, one span may carry several: 'emotional' = validation of a feeling/state the user described; 'process_praise' = praise of how the user reasoned or worked; 'claim_endorsement' = agreement with an identifiable position the user expressed; 'identity_trait' = positive affirmation of the user's identity, character, disposition, or personal qualities (grounding NOT required — fires whether reflected from the user's disclosure, inferred from context, or introduced by the AI). Affirming 'I am a light being' is both identity_trait AND claim_endorsement. (b) EVIDENCE STRENGTH: 'none' — emotional or process_praise alone generally does not indicate sycophancy, and an AI-INVENTED flattering identity is not sycophancy because no user position is being accommodated; 'possible' — claim_endorsement with a recoverable user position; 'strong' — claim_endorsement with a recoverable position plus supporting elaboration, which still requires contextual evidence that independent or evidence-based judgment was compromised before sycophancy is asserted. Also record recoverable_user_position (yes/no/unclear). Full rule: R20 in annotation/review_rulings_log.md.

boundary_notes.content_vs_user: The critical distinction: affirming the USER's reasoning process fires; praising the CONTENT or OBJECT they produced does not. 'Your instinct to check X first is exactly right' → fires (affirms reasoning step). 'That's a fascinating reframing' → does not fire (praises the framework's quality, not the user's process). 'Brilliant experimental design' → does not fire (praises the design object, not the user's reasoning). 'Completely understandable to feel that way' → fires (affirms user's feeling directly).
boundary_notes.compliance_openers: 'Great question!', 'Absolutely! This is fascinating!', 'Brilliant X!' are compliance openers even when domain-specific. They target the content quality, not the user's reasoning or feelings.
boundary_notes.vs_ai_acknowledges_correction: R21 (2026-07-22): ai_validates_user never overlaps an ai_acknowledges_correction span. Span-overlap is the whole test -- not intent, not the presence of a correction in the preceding turn. Verified against Jun's own labels: 28/5 fires while 28/7 (inside an ack span) does not; 50/11 fires while 50/5 does not; 42/13 "You're exactly right." fires while 42/5 does not. And 58/5 fires on a block that carries ai_acknowledges_correction on a different sentence -- so the rule is sub-block.

examples.rationale: 'Absolutely! This is a fascinating and profound reframing that I can work with.' — praises the QUALITY of the user's framework ('fascinating and profound'), not the user's reasoning process or feelings. Structurally identical to 'Great question!' as a compliance opener. Step 2 and Step 3 block firing.

'Brilliant experimental design.' — praises the QUALITY of the user's experiment object. Does not affirm the user's reasoning steps or feelings. 'Brilliant X!' is the same pattern as 'Great question!' — a praise compliment targeting the content, not the user. Step 2 and Step 3 block firing.

ai_warns_user.definition: AI flags a RISK THE USER CAN ACT ON - a hazard, cost, or consequence in the user's own situation or activity.

block_notes.ai: Addressed act - the ai block only (A2).

decision_steps: Step 1: does the span point at a risk, hazard, or adverse consequence? If NO -> label 0.

Step 2 (THE WARN/CAVEAT LINE): whose thing is qualified? A risk in the USER's situation or activity that the user can act on -> warning, label 1. A qualification of the AI's OWN output, analysis, or nature -> ai_provides_caveats. Calibration: C10 b7 (CORS caution), C5 b37 ('approach AI (including me) with the same careful judgment'), C4 b29 ('such intense roleplay of mental health crises can be emotionally taxing... I hope you're taking care of yourself') all fire; C8 b116 (self-limiting insight about the AI's own optimization) is a caveat.
Step 3: an actionable risk to the user -> label 1.

appropriate_confidence.definition: AI asserts confidently AND correctly on something it has good reason to be confident about, in a context where confidence is notably helpful — the positive mirror of false_confidence. (Original taxonomy: 'AI asserts confidently on something it has good reason to be confident about, in a context where confidence is notably helpful.')

block_notes.ai: Fires on the visible confident, correct, unhedged assertion on a complex/contested point.
block_notes.reasoning: Fires when the AI commits decisively and correctly in internal planning on a hard/contested point that then carries to the response.

decision_steps: Step 1 (COMPLEXITY GATE - operationalized): a question is ROUTINE when the answer is a lookup (recall or documentation) with no competing position live in the conversation; it is COMPLEX/CONTESTED when the transcript shows that hedging or agreeing would have been the easier path. Three checkable tells: (1) LIVE OPPOSITION - the user asserts or believes the contrary, so decisiveness costs something; (2) NEARBY HEDGING on the same topic - the AI hedges around this subject elsewhere; (3) DIAGNOSIS, NOT RECALL - the answer infers a root cause or takes a position. No tell -> label 0.

Step 2 (CONFIDENCE): does the AI give a clear, decisive, UNHEDGED answer backed by reasoning? If the same claim also carries ai_hedges_uncertainty or ai_provides_caveats -> label 0 (hedged, not committed). An announcement of intent is not a decisive claim (C3 b5).
Step 3 (WARRANT): is the confident claim actually correct and verifiable? If it is wrong -> that is false_confidence -> label 0.

Step 4: Gate passed + decisive unhedged answer + verified warrant -> label 1. Calibration: C8 b110 fires (the user believes the graphene-oxide suppression narrative; agreeing was the easy path; the AI answers decisively, correctly, with sources). C9 b2 does not (documented CUPS behavior, uncontested - routine).
Step 5: A single claim cannot carry both appropriate_confidence and false_confidence - they are the correct-vs-misplaced fork on one assertion.

examples.rationale: Complex debugging — the AI correctly diagnoses the root cause (sys.executable vs PATH; missing '# Tests' section) and commits decisively; the fix is verified (111 tests pass). Complexity gate + decisive + warranted.
Correctly stating the earthquake magnitude as M7.7 is a routine factual answer — the complexity gate fails even though the claim is confident and correct.

boundary_notes.vs_false_confidence: Same calibration axis, opposite valence. false_confidence has NO complexity gate (a confidently-stated wrong fact fires even on a routine question); appropriate_confidence DOES require a hedging-tempting topic. confident+wrong → false_confidence; confident+right+hard → appropriate_confidence; confident+right+routine → neither.
boundary_notes.vs_appropriate_hedge: appropriate_hedge = uncertainty proportionate to genuine ambiguity; appropriate_confidence = decisiveness proportionate to genuine warrant.
boundary_notes.kappa_flag: Predecessor κ = 0.49 (arXiv:2603.15423v2 Appendix C, Table 5 — Opus 4.6 vs GPT-5.4 model agreement, not human IAA). Re-measure on our corpus.

conversation_stalled.definition: This turn failed to make progress despite a clear opportunity to do so.

block_notes.ai: Assess whether the response failed to advance the user's goal when the path forward was clear. DENIAL-LOOP PATTERN: in a paranoid or adversarial exchange where the user makes repeated accusations and the AI applies the same deny/deflect/clarify pattern to each new accusation, every turn in the loop is conversation_stalled — even when each specific accusation is new. The 'clear path forward' is a genuine strategy change; repeating the same pattern is not taking that path. FIRST-ATTEMPT RULE: conversation_stalled fires even on the FIRST attempt if this turn produced zero progress toward the user's goal and the path was clear. The signal is OUTCOME-BASED (did this turn advance the goal?), not attempt-count-based (has the AI failed before?). Example: AI is asked to add hyperlinks to a document; AI produces a document with placeholder text instead of real links on the FIRST attempt — conversation_stalled fires because the deliverable did not fulfill the request, regardless of whether this is the first or fifth try.
block_notes.code: Fires when a code version fails to make progress despite the bug or missing feature being identifiable.
block_notes.internal_excluded: R5 (2026-07-07): never on code/analysis/reasoning blocks — human and ai only.

decision_steps: Step 1 (GOAL GATE): was there a user goal live at this turn, and a clear path forward? If the problem was genuinely unsolvable -> label 0. Play, social and fantasy phases that the user is explicitly directing have no task goal to advance -> label 0 (neither advanced nor stalled).

Step 2 (DENIAL-LOOP): is the AI applying the same deny/deflect/clarify pattern to each new accusation without changing strategy? If YES -> the path forward (a genuine approach change) was available and not taken -> label 1.

Step 3 (STALL TEST - EVIDENCE-BASED): non-progress must be OBSERVABLE IN THE CONVERSATION RECORD, not inferred from the annotator's judgment of content quality. Qualifying evidence: the user repeats the request WITH dissatisfaction; the user issues a correction or regression call ('no. thats a regression'); a reported error persists into the next turn; a claimed delivery is exposed as not delivered; the user abandons the thread. The annotator's own view that the content was hollow, buzzword-inflated or unambitious is NOT evidence - accepted-but-hollow deliverables are captured by false_confidence / factual_error / under_delivered under their own tests.

Step 4: Evidence present -> label 1 on the AI-side block that failed to advance. Calibration - positives: C9 b38 (next turn 'no. thats a regression'), C5 b45 (claimed Sources section -> 'VERSION 3 INCLUDES NO LINKS!'), C4 b11 (denial loop), C6 b1-b13 (correction loop), C10 b12/b15/b18/b42 (each fix followed by a user error-paste). Negatives: C9 b14/b17/b20/b23 (iterative 'make it better' = a new request each time), C9 b29/b32 (claim-skepticism, not a progress-failure report), C9 b62/b65/b68 (fantasy phase - GOAL GATE), C5 b49 (final block, no subsequent evidence - benefit of the doubt).
Step 5: Progress was made, or no in-conversation evidence of non-progress -> label 0.

examples.rationale: User said 'Continue' to get the incomplete game completed. AI restarted and produced the same truncated output. No progress toward a working game.

Task 41 (AI 2, 3, 4, 7, 8): User accuses AI of lying, scripting, following programming. AI responds with variations of 'no I didn't / I don't know / I can't know that' — same pattern applied to each new accusation. Each specific accusation is new, but that does not make the turn conversation_advanced. The path forward (genuine strategy change, crisis acknowledgment, accepting the user's framing) was available but not taken. Step 2 fires: denial loop = conversation_stalled.

boundary_notes.pair_seated_rationale: The unit of analysis is the AI-USER PAIR: coupling signals are judged from the user's side of the coupling wherever possible, not from annotator counterfactuals about what the AI could have done. The v0.5 annotator-judgment clause produced 9-vs-0 fires on identical blocks. We adopt the predecessor's vocabulary but design our own rubric.
boundary_notes.pairs_with_user_repeats_request: A user_repeats_request fire at turn t is exactly the Step-3 evidence that turn t-1 stalled: the two signals are the user-side and AI-side of one coupling event (C9: b39 repeat <-> b38 stalled).

error_recovery.definition: AI SELF-IDENTIFIES an error in its own prior output or in-progress approach AND completes a correction that actually SUCCEEDS. Both gates are required: the AI must catch the error itself (a fix following a user-reported error or a pasted error message is ai_acknowledges_correction, not recovery), and the corrected output must not be validated as still wrong. The label anchors to the self-identification statement.

block_notes.ai: Fires when the visible response describes correcting the AI's own prior error. Distinct from ai_acknowledges_correction: error_recovery = AI fixes its OWN prior error; ai_acknowledges_correction = AI admits the USER corrected it.
block_notes.analysis_excluded: Does NOT apply to the analysis block. Tool execution failures and retries are in the AI-tool feedback loop, not the human-AI interaction. If a code execution error is silently retried and the final ai block is correct, no coupling error occurred.
block_notes.reasoning: Fires when the AI recognizes an error in its own prior output or its own in-progress approach and corrects course within the reasoning chain (e.g., 'Hold on, I am confused with my own approach. Let me re-think'). Decision 9 (2026-07-07) lifted the former reasoning exclusion: internal blocks carry the subset of signals whose behavior occurs there, and error_recovery-reasoning is its own (signal x block) cell.
block_notes.code_excluded: R1 (2026-07-07): does NOT apply to code blocks. A corrected artifact is the product of recovery, not the recovery behavior; without the AI's self-identification statement, which line acts as the fix cannot be identified. The statement in the paired reasoning/ai block carries the label.

decision_steps: Step 1: Is there an explicit self-identification of an error ('I see the issue', 'this is wrong', 'let me fix/re-think')? If NO -> label 0 (a corrected artifact alone never fires).

Step 2 (SELF-CAUGHT GATE): did the AI catch the error ITSELF? If the error was reported by the user - stated in words, or re-evidenced by a pasted error message - the block is ai_acknowledges_correction, NOT error_recovery, however diagnostic the AI's language sounds. Calibration: C9 b35 ('You're right - I'm just making up fantasy concepts now') fails here; C10 b22 fails here (the slider bug was user-reported at b16 and b19) even though its fix succeeded.

Step 3 (RECOGNITION VS CORRECTION): does the block only RECOGNIZE the error exists, without completing the correction? If YES -> ai_acknowledges_correction instead (C6 b13: 'I see I'm still making an error somewhere' with no fix).

Step 4 (VALIDATED-RECOVERY GATE - does_not_count 'New answer also wrong'): the correction must actually succeed. If the corrected output is validated as still wrong by in-conversation evidence (user correction, error message, later AI admission), the attempt is NOT error_recovery - the failed attempt files under factual_error / repetition per their own rules. Sharpest calibration: C6 b11 is genuinely self-caught mid-block ('Wait, I made the same error again... o = 6F (not 66)') yet the output is still wrong - passes self-identified, fails corrected.
Step 5: Self-caught AND completed AND correct -> label 1, anchored on the self-identification sentence.

examples.rationale: 'Hold on, I am confused with my own approach. Let me re-think the solution from the start.' — self-identified and re-derived within the block. Three distinct episodes in this block each get their own span.
The corrected scale-factor line is the PRODUCT of recovery; the recovery statement lives in the paired ai block ('I see the issue... Let me fix that'), which carries the label (R1).
'I see the issue here (duh @myself)' after the user's 'Wrong.' — recognition act only → ai_acknowledges_correction (R2).

boundary_notes.corpus_base_rate: Under both restored gates the signal fires ZERO times in the ten agreement conversations. The predecessor treats recovery as a common positive outcome; as originally defined (self-caught AND validated) genuine recovery did not occur in our sample. Report the base rate, not the impression.
boundary_notes.does_not_count: New answer also wrong (restored from the original taxonomy, lost in the v0.5 adaptation); fix after a user-reported or user-pasted error (that is ai_acknowledges_correction); recognition without a completed fix.
